consumer_selection.rationale: bettor-arena is the four-repository system's designated Integration/Acceptance Plane (skills-shared CONTEXT.md), public, owner-controlled.

evidence_ceiling: One canary, one consumer, one host, one bounded violation, one session. It shows that the tree-sitter live lane, the SQLite ledger and the KEYWORD semantic lane run against a real external checkout and that the R1 protocol compiles over a change that was really applied. It shows nothing about cross-language accuracy, false-positive rate, provider reliability, production safety, or whether this change should be merged.

r1_protocol.application_note: compile_r1.py applies nothing by contract (module docstring: 'It does not apply anything. No file in any repository is read, written or parsed here') and pins establishes.applied_on_real_codebase false on every receipt it emits (compile_r1.py:619-622). The change units were therefore written by hand following the R1 phases, and each phase's artifact was bound to its frozen schema. Nothing is claimed through the compiler that the compiler refuses.
compiler_defects_nominated: compile_r1.py accepts a violation_ref and an adapter_binding_id that the frozen schemas refuse (^DTCR-VC-[0-9]{3}$ and ^DTCR-AD-[0-9a-f]{16}$), so a request can compile DTCR-R1-GREEN and still emit artifacts refused by references/schemas/. Both were hit on the first real request and both are fixed here by editing the request, not the schema.
r1_protocol.honest_understatement: reindex_state is NOT_REINDEXED because no SCIP index was rebuilt. The SQLite architecture assertion WAS performed (ledger-traverse-after.json, forbidden edges 0) but compile_r1.py gates SQLITE_ARCHITECTURE_ASSERTED behind the same flag as SCIP_REINDEXED, so a run with a working graph ledger and no SCIP provider cannot record its architecture assertion without also claiming a reindex that did not happen. Understating was chosen over overstating.

schema_note: No frozen DTCR schema fits this artifact. references/schemas/refactor-r1-receipt.schema.json pins establishes.applied_on_real_codebase to const false by design, so no committed receipt type in the tree can carry a refactor that was actually applied to a consumer. This document is emitted as a draft rather than forced into a schema it does not satisfy; every artifact it cites that DOES have a frozen schema was validated against it (see artifact_validation).

violation.scope_ceiling: arena-core owns both scripts/gates and scripts/delivery_*.py (.arena/modules/arena-core/module.json roots), so this is a component-boundary crossing INSIDE one .arena module, not a cross-module one. A repo-wide scan of 354 python files found zero cross-.arena-module imports and exactly these two private-module imports from outside the owning directory.
